hook: Their heart beats twelve hundred times a minute.
caption:
Their heart beats twelve hundred times a minute.

A hummingbird is the only bird that can hover in still air, sustaining a wingbeat of fifty cycles per second by burning sugar so fast that any individual bird is two hours from starvation at any given moment. To make a single migration across the Gulf of Mexico, a Ruby-throated hummingbird doubles its body weight in fat, then flies five hundred miles in a single non-stop crossing. The species's collapse is not loud: agricultural neonicotinoid pesticides accumulate in flower nectar at concentrations that disrupt hummingbird memory and navigation, climate shifts have pulled bloom times out of sync with northbound migration, and Audubon's Climate Watch found that fifteen North American hummingbird species could lose more than half their breeding range by 2080 under current emissions. The smallest bird in the hemisphere is also the most numerically fragile.
